Apple spray schedule by stage

By Gafar Laiya, Gujarat Bio Organics · Updated 2026-11-25

Spray apple by stage and by need, not by calendar. The key points are: horticultural mineral oil (2%) at delayed dormant above 4°C; scab protection from green tip in wet weather; boron at pink bud; no sprays at full bloom; calcium chloride sprays from 2–3 weeks after petal fall; Marssonina, Alternaria and mite watch in the monsoon; no sprays 3–4 weeks before picking; and urea + zinc + boron at leaf fall. Use the doses in your state's current schedule (SKUAST-K 2026, Dr. YSP UHF).

A November 2026 survey found only about 25% of Kashmir growers following the SKUAST-K schedule, while spending Rs 97,360–1,09,870 per hectare on pesticides. Calendar spraying kills predatory Typhlodromus mites and causes European red mite outbreaks, so growers then spray even more.

Stage-wise spray guide

StageMain targetWhat the schedules useNotes
Dormant (Dec–Feb)Canker, scale eggsCopper paste on cuts; whitewash trunks (Nov)Prune and paste the same day
Delayed dormant / silver tip (Feb–Mar)San Jose scale, mite eggsHorticultural mineral oil 2%Only above 4°C; keep 14–21 days apart from sulphur
Green tip to tight cluster (Mar)Apple scabProtectant fungicide in wet weather (e.g. captan, mancozeb, dodine)Rotate fungicide groups
Pink bud (Mar–Apr)Fruit set; thrips; scabBoron 0.1–0.15%; thrips control only pre-bloomLast chance before bloom
Full bloom (Apr)PollinationNothingBees at work; 4–6 hives per hectare
Petal fall to pea size (Apr–May)Scab, powdery mildew; thinningFungicide rotation (e.g. difenoconazole, myclobutanil); thinners only as advisedThin within 10–25 days after petal fall
Fruit development (May–Aug)Bitter pit; Marssonina, Alternaria; red miteCalcium chloride 0.3–0.5% (4–6 sprays, 15 days apart); rotated fungicides (e.g. zineb/propineb, ziram, metiram + pyraclostrobin, tebuconazole + trifloxystrobin); acaricides only above thresholdNo calcium chloride above 28–30°C; separate calcium from sulphates and phosphates
Pre-harvest (Aug–Oct)Pre-harvest dropNAA 10 ppm 10–20 days before expected drop, if neededStop other sprays 3–4 weeks before picking
Leaf fall (Oct–Nov)Bud reload; scab carry-over3–5% urea + 0.5% zinc sulphate + 0.1–0.2% Solubor; copper clean-upSpray while leaves are still green

Pesticide safety: Use only pesticides registered for apple by CIB&RC, at the dose and waiting period on the label, and follow your state's current spray schedule (SKUAST-K, Dr. YSP UHF or the state horticulture department). This table shows stages and active ingredients named in the SKUAST-K and Dr. YSP UHF schedules; always take doses and intervals from the current official schedule and the product label.

How to cut your spray bill

  • Spray for a reason: scout first (10× lens for mites, leaf spots after rain).
  • Do not spray pyrethroids by calendar; they kill predatory mites.
  • Keep the canopy open and rake or rot fallen leaves to cut scab and Marssonina.
  • Never mix calcium sprays with sulphates or phosphates; never spray sulphur within 14–21 days of oil.

Questions farmers ask

What is the apple spray schedule for 2026?

Follow your state's official schedule (SKUAST-K 2026 for Kashmir; Dr. YSP UHF / Himachal horticulture department). The stages are dormant oil, scab protection from green tip, pink-bud boron, no sprays at bloom, calcium and leaf-disease sprays in summer, and urea + zinc + boron at leaf fall.

Should I spray apple during flowering?

No. Never spray at full bloom: it kills bees and harms pollination.

Why are red mites increasing in my orchard?

Calendar spraying of pyrethroids kills the predatory mites that keep red mite under control. Spray only when needed and rotate acaricide groups.

Can I mix sulphur and oil sprays?

No. Keep wettable sulphur and horticultural mineral oil 14–21 days apart.
